findings.source_passage: Night beat me to the stoop of my apartment building, and with it came its friends shadow and darkness.
findings.why_it_matters: The personification 'its friends shadow and darkness' is a small but rhythmically distinctive piece of voice-establishing prose; the draft drops 'its friends' and substitutes 'silence,' erasing both the rhetorical figure and the narrator's wry tone.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'its friends shadow and darkness' verbatim in the opening paragraph.

findings.source_passage: Hulking shadows of trashcans and broken boxes stared back at me. Puddles reflected the darkness that was only broken by a few feeble attempts by the streetlights to illuminate the deep interior.
findings.why_it_matters: The personification 'stared back at me' and the wryly hyperbolic 'feeble attempts by the streetlights to illuminate the deep interior' both carry the narrator's signature ironic register; the draft compresses this to a flat list ('Boxes, cans, a few feeble streetlights reflecting off puddles') stripping both the stare-personification and the extended metaphor.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'hulking shadows…stared back at me' and the 'feeble attempts by the streetlights' phrasing to preserve the alley's menacing-yet-wry character.

findings.source_passage: My furious thoughts gave way to a loose grasp of consciousness. My head began to spin along with the room. In a moment I was knocked clean out.
findings.why_it_matters: 'My furious thoughts' and 'a loose grasp of consciousness' establish interior resistance and are tonally distinct; the source's three-beat closing ('furious thoughts / loose grasp / knocked clean out') is a recognizable rhythmic close. The draft renders it as 'Thoughts unraveled; the room tilted. Darkness took me cleanly.' — a poetic substitute that erases the specific 'furious thoughts' interiority and the colloquial 'knocked clean out.'
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'My furious thoughts gave way to a loose grasp of consciousness' and the colloquial closing 'knocked clean out' to preserve both the interior voice and the chapter's tonal landing.

findings.source_passage: My one-bedroom apartment was on the third floor with a lovely view of the fire escape and the neighboring brick building.
findings.why_it_matters: The dry irony of 'a lovely view of the fire escape and the neighboring brick building' is a small character beat; the draft substitutes 'a friendly brick wall,' losing 'lovely view' and compressing the joke.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'a lovely view of the fire escape and the neighboring brick building' to keep the narrator's self-deprecating irony intact.

findings.source_passage: Its only reaction was tears that pooled in my eyes and slid down my cheeks.
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'its only reaction' distancing Miriam from her own body is an interpretively important moment of helpless dissociation; the draft has 'Tears slid from my unblinking eyes,' which conveys the image but loses the dissociative grammar that makes the paralysis vivid.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the subject-shift 'Its only reaction was tears that pooled in my eyes' to preserve the bodily-dissociation effect.

summary: No high-severity signature losses; two medium-severity voice flattenings (alley personification and closing interiority) and three low-severity irony/register erosions are present but insufficient individually to mandate regeneration under the rubric.
